phases.text:
You let the breath out and lower the cane — and the nest answers you, two more rats spilling wet out of the bank, and behind them something old and heavy drags itself into the light while the dog spins back around, hackles up again.

You catch one of the rats with the cane and it staggers back, wounded.

The dog gets its teeth into the other and worries it hard.

A rat snaps at the dog and misses.

The other rat catches the dog's leg and it yelps.

The Nest Warden heaves, and a third rat comes spilling out of the nest behind it, then goes still, drained.

The new rat lunges at the dog and doesn't connect.

You strike the wounded rat again and it reels.

The dog snaps at the other rat and connects, shaking it hard.

A rat goes for the dog and misses.

Another rat lunges for the dog and misses too.

The Nest Warden still hasn't moved.

The third rat snaps at the dog and comes up short.

You bring the cane down on the rat again, and it's barely standing.

The dog goes for the other rat and misses.

A rat gets its teeth into the dog's side.

Another rat bites down on the dog too, and it staggers.

The Nest Warden remains frozen.

The third rat snaps at the dog and misses.

You swing at the rat and it's already darting clear.

The dog catches it and it goes limp, finished.

A rat tears into the dog and it goes down hard, and doesn't rise again.

The Nest Warden lunges past where the dog fell and catches you instead, hard.

A rat turns on you now and misses.

You swing at a rat and it slips past the cane.

A rat lunges at you and misses.

The Nest Warden drives into you, and it staggers you back.

Another rat gets its teeth into your leg.

You catch a rat square and it drops back, badly hurt.

A rat bites at you and connects, quick and low.

The Nest Warden swings for you and misses.

Another rat sinks its teeth in again.

You strike the rat again, and it's nearly done.

A rat goes for you and misses.

The Nest Warden swings and doesn't find you.

A rat lunges and misses too.

You catch the rat hard, and it reels.

A rat snaps at you and misses.

The Nest Warden swings again and misses.

Another rat gets in and bites you.

You strike the rat once more.

A rat lunges for you and misses.

The Nest Warden swings and misses again.

Another rat bites down on you.

Your foot slides on the blood-slick grass and the swing you meant for the rat goes wide.

A rat goes for you and misses.

The Nest Warden catches you hard, driving you back.

A rat lunges and misses.

You swing again and miss.

A rat gets its teeth into you.

The Nest Warden swings and doesn't connect.

Another rat lunges and misses.

You swing again and miss.

A rat bites down on you.

The Nest Warden catches you solidly, and pain roars up your side.

Another rat lunges for you and misses.

You wrench free of all of it and run, the fog swallowing you whole.

note: The dog is still with her, bloodied from the Rat Mother — give it 6 health of 12. The nest is not empty: two more come boiling out of the bank, and behind them something older drags itself into the light. Declare the fight now, do not narrate it. them: two Marsh Rats (6 health, 1-2 damage, dc 10, bonus 1) and the Nest Warden (16 health, 2-4 damage, dc 12, bonus 2) with an ability that spawns one more Marsh Rat and then leaves it not stirring for 2 rounds. us: the dog (6 health of 12, 1-3 damage, dc 12, bonus 2). athletics, their_dc 11, flee_dc 10.

proposal.summary: You lower the cane and let your breath out, sure the Rat Mother is finished.

outcomes.text: Before you can step back, the bank tears open again — two more Marsh Rats boil out, and behind them the Nest Warden drags itself into the light; the dog, bloodied, is already turning to meet them.
The nest isn't done — two Marsh Rats spill out where the Rat Mother fell, and something larger hauls itself out behind them as the dog snarls back around.
The Nest Warden heaves as it emerges and a third rat comes spilling out with it, then goes rigid and still — one more body in the fight than you counted.
The Rat Mother's body slumps back across the nest mouth, and the two rats and the Warden have to climb over her to reach you, buying a half-step before they're on you.
The Nest Warden's hide, catching the light, carries markings too regular to be natural — cut lines, not scars, in a pattern no bestiary you've read describes.
What the Nest Warden drags in behind it isn't rat-boned at all — the shape under the fur is too long, too old, jointed like it was laid there on purpose for something to find.
